name: Blood Gas Analyzer (Generic)
description: Measures acid-base balance, electrolytes, and blood gases in clinical specimens.
parameters: pCO2 - Partial pressure of carbon dioxide
troubleshooting: Air bubbles in sample: Expel immediately, samples are anaerobic
Delayed analysis: Re-analyze if delay > 15 minutes, apply ice bath if delays unavoidable
Calibration drift: Perform 2-point calibration before critical samples
Out-of-range results: Verify electrode function, check standard solutions
notes: Critical for ICU and emergency departments. Understand acid-base compensation mechanisms for clinical interpretation.

name: Gastat700 Series
description: Advanced blood gas analyzer for rapid acid-base, electrolyte, and blood gas measurement. Comprehensive field guide with full operational details and maintenance procedures.
parameters: pCO2 - Partial pressure of carbon dioxide
troubleshooting: Air bubbles in sample: Remove immediately, maintain anaerobic conditions
Delayed analysis: Apply ice bath if analysis delay > 15 minutes
Calibration errors: Verify calibrator function and electrode performance
Out-of-range results: Check electrode calibration and sample quality
Temperature variations: Maintain consistent sample and analyzer temperature
Pressure discrepancies: Verify barometric pressure setting
notes: Professional blood gas analyzer designed for clinical laboratory and point-of-care testing. Provides comprehensive acid-base, electrolyte, and metabolite analysis. Includes full field guide with operational procedures, maintenance protocols, and troubleshooting guidance. Critical for ICU, emergency, and respiratory departments.

name: Bricyte E6
description: Automated hematology analyzer with Flow Cytometry. Suitable for clinical laboratories and hospital settings.
parameters: WBC - Total White Blood Cell Count
troubleshooting: Cold sample: Warm to room temperature (18-25°C) before analysis
Clotted sample: Discard, recollect in proper anticoagulant (EDTA K2)
Low platelet count: Verify no clumping, review blood smear
Instrument error E001: Check reagent bottles and perform purge cycle
Abnormal WBC differential: Review with microscope for morphology assessment
High NTU (turbidity): Check for hemolysis or lipemia, recollect if necessary
No aspiration: Verify sample level in tube, check sampling needle is clear
notes: Flow Cytometry Analyzer of Mindray. Compatible with EDTA / Heparin anticoagulated whole blood specimens. Results include complete CBC with differential and RBC/platelet indices. Regular maintenance and calibration required for optimal performance.

name: Mindray CX Series
description: Advanced coagulation analyzer series with models CX-6000, CX-6100, and CX-9000. Complete training hub with comprehensive measurement principles, specifications, QC management, troubleshooting, and setup guides.
parameters: Factor Assays (V, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII)
troubleshooting: Probe Clog: Run Sample Probe Unclog from Maintenance menu
Wash Solution Exhausted: Replace wash solution container and run Tube Prime
Waste Container Full: Empty biohazard waste container safely
Invalid QC Result: Check QC material lot, expiration date, and storage temperature
Temperature Alarm: Verify power supply and airflow, cool system 15 minutes, restart
Barcode Not Scanned: Clean scanner window, verify barcode clarity, check sample positioning
Measurement Error: Verify reagent reconstitution, check sample quality, review calibration
notes: High-precision coagulation testing using optical clot detection (OCD) methodology. All models include Westgard QC rules, LIS integration, RFID support, and comprehensive measurement principle documentation. Optical measurement principle tracks plasma turbidity change during coagulation for accurate clot detection. Daily maintenance is critical for accuracy and preventing carryover contamination. Supports both 3.2% sodium citrate and alternative anticoagulants.

name: TOSOH HLC-723G11
description: High-performance glycohemoglobin analyzer for HbA1c measurement using HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography) technology. Supports STD and VAR analysis modes with advanced peak detection.
parameters: STD ANALYSIS Mode - Standard analysis for routine hemoglobin samples
VAR ANALYSIS Mode - Variant analysis for abnormal hemoglobin detection
Total Area - Chromatography integration quality indicator
Hemoglobin Fractions (FP, A1A, A1B, A1C, F, A0)
Peak Detection - Advanced identification of unknown peaks
troubleshooting: AREA TOO LOW (<500): Re-dilute sample at 1:100 using STAT INCREASE mode
AREA LOW (500-700): Monitor sample preparation and concentration
AREA HIGH (3000-3500): Re-dilute sample at 1:400 using STAT DECREASE mode
AREA TOO HIGH (>3500): Must re-dilute and re-assay immediately
PRESSURE HIGH (>2 MPa): Check and replace filter after ~600 samples
PRESSURE LOW: Verify buffer levels, execute DRAIN FLUSH procedure
CALIB ERROR (>0.3% deviation): Check calibrator/buffer lot matching, verify column condition
NOT DETECT [peak]: Check buffer concentration, column age, sample quality
TP LOW/TOO LOW: May indicate column degradation or variant hemoglobin patient
notes: Highly reliable HbA1c measurement system suitable for diabetes management and screening. Acceptable TOTAL AREA range is 300-1,800 (optimal: 400-1,700). Calibration required before patient sample analysis. Filter replacement at ~600 samples, column replacement at ~2,500 samples. Supports both NGSP and IFCC units.

HIL Detection - Hemolysis, Ictorus, Lipemia qualitative & quantitative measurement

Supports flexible modular combination of chemistry and immunoassay for maximum laboratory productivity. Includes quantitative HIL detection (Hemolysis, Ictorus, Lipemia) without additional reagents. Ideal for core laboratories requiring scalable capacity and fast turnaround time with improved patient care quality.

name: Re-exam Rule update for EU series
description: Urine re-exam rule set for the EU series (EU8600 rule file, 2026-09-19): 40 rules grouped by purpose, with RBC/WBC and other sediment conditions shown in real counts (cells/HPF or LPF) and dipstick results as grades.
parameters: Strip vs sediment mismatch - BLD/RBC and LEU/WBC deviation rules
RBC morphology / interference - dysmorphic, acanthocyte, humped RBC, Vitamin C
Protein vs casts - hyaline and pathological casts with negative protein, Precise PRO
Appearance / SG / ketone - turbidity, low SG, ketone
Positive / above-reference flags - LEU, BLD, RBC, WBC, HYAC, CRYS
Particle detected - non-squamous epithelial, macrophage, cast types
troubleshooting: Too many re-exam flags: review the broad rules 24-30 (positive / above-reference)
Rule never fires: check the level numbers against the analyzer level tables
Redundant rules (covered by another): 3 by 2, 5 by 8, 6 by 7, 13 by 12, 16 by 17
Precise PRO (rule 31): protein 2+ or higher triggers re-exam with precise mode (SEDIMP)
notes: All conditions in a rule are combined with AND; a fired rule flags the sample for re-exam and shows its message. Rules apply to all samples (no include/exclude filters). Turbidity level names are not confirmed.
